newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam widens forex band, rules out devaluation. [CORRECTED 02:33 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Vietnam widens forex band, rules out devaluation. [CORRECTED 02:33 GMT]

text.p: The State Bank of Vietnam has widened the official interbank trading band for the dong to 10 percent around its pivot rate from two percent (corrects from five percent), an official at the central bank's foreign exchange department said on Monday.

Dealers said the move would allow pent-up demand for U.S. dollars to push the national currency lower. However, State Bank Governor Cao Si Kiem told the Dau Tu weekly that the authorities were managing the currency, not aiming to devalue it.
"The State Bank's view is that there should be no devaluation," the official Dau Tu newspaper quoted Kiem as saying.

"The State Bank will continue managing the exchange rate according to market supply and demand to encourage exports, control imports, increase foreign currency reserves, maintain a healthy balance of payments and ensure macroeconomic stability," he added.

The Bank's official rate was set at 11,096 per dollar on Monday, which put its floor at 11,650 and its ceiling at 10,542. At the end of last week the dong was quoted at its old floor of 11,208 per dollar.
Traders said the dong was bid at 11,220 on Monday morning, though trading was thin.
